sentences.en: KIERAN: So Jane - you'll be off to Denmark soon to do your work placement.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 那么简——你很快就要动身去丹麦进行实习了。

sentences.en: JANE: Yes.
sentences.zh: JANE: 是的。

sentences.en: I'm really looking forward to it and I've just started packing up all my books to put in storage.
sentences.zh: 我真的很期待这次行程，而且刚刚开始把所有书打包存起来。

sentences.en: KIERAN: Well. hope they don't get spoilt.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 嗯，希望它们不会受损。

sentences.en: JANE: It's OK - my grandfather works in a bookshop and he told me how to pack them.
sentences.zh: JANE: 没问题——我祖父在一家书店工作，他教过我该怎么打包。

sentences.en: KIERAN: Oh, that's helpful.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 哦，这很有帮助。

sentences.en: JANE: He says you have to support the spine otherwise the paper can come away from the cover.
sentences.zh: JANE: 他说必须支撑住书脊，否则纸张会从封面脱落。

sentences.en: KIERAN: Yeah - that's obvious.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 嗯——这很明显。

sentences.en: JANE: He also told me to pack them flat in the box not on their side again because they can bend and if you leave them like that for, say, a year, it's quite hard to get them back to their normal shape.
sentences.zh: JANE: 他还告诉我，要把书平放在箱子里，而不是侧放，因为侧放会导致书本弯曲；如果你就这样放上一年左右，就很难让它们恢复原状了。

sentences.en: KIERAN: Well, it's pretty clear that ruins them, but a lot of people just can't be bothered to protect their books.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 嗯，这显然会毁掉书本，但很多人就是懒得好好保护自己的书。

sentences.en: JANE: He always says it's such a shame that publishers don't use better-quality paper.
sentences.zh: JANE: 他总说，出版商不使用更高质量的纸张，真是令人遗憾。

sentences.en: KIERAN: It's the acid in the paper that causes the problem, isn't it?
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 纸张中的酸性物质才是造成问题的原因，对吧？

sentences.en: JANE: Yeah - that's why old books go yellow.
sentences.zh: JANE: 对——这就是为什么旧书会变黄。

sentences.en: You know some of the books my grandfather's given me are like that already.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我祖父给我的一些书已经变成那样了。

sentences.en: KIERAN: Oh . . .
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 哦……

sentences.en: JANE: I should dump them really if they're going to deteriorate further, but I'd feel bad.
sentences.zh: JANE: 如果这些书还会继续恶化，我其实真该把它们扔掉，但我会觉得于心不忍。

sentences.en: They'll always remind me of him.
sentences.zh: 它们总会让我想起他。

sentences.en: He's quite a collector, you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他可是个相当资深的藏书家。

sentences.en: KIERAN: Well, if they're important to you ..
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 嗯，如果它们对你来说很重要……

sentences.en: JANE: Yeah - I'd regret just throwing them away.
sentences.zh: JANE: 是啊——我肯定会后悔就这么把它们丢掉。

sentences.en: KIERAN: You know, maybe it's because I was taught to treasure books . .. but I hate seeing students force open the pages of paperbacks.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 你知道吗，也许是因为我从小就被教导要珍惜书籍……但我特别讨厌看到学生们粗暴地掰开平装书的书页。

sentences.en: They press so hard they end up breaking the spine.
sentences.zh: 他们用力过猛，结果常常把书脊弄断。

sentences.en: JANE: I know, but unfortunately, paperbacks aren't designed to last a long time and people know that.
sentences.zh: JANE: 我知道，但不幸的是，平装书本来就没打算长期保存，大家心里都清楚这一点。

sentences.en: Hardbacks aren't quite as weak.
sentences.zh: 精装书则没那么脆弱。

sentences.en: KIERAN: Yeah, they're different, suppose.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 嗯，它们确实不一样，我想也是。

sentences.en: But I still don't think people value hardbacks like they used to.
sentences.zh: 但我仍然觉得，人们不像过去那样珍视精装书了。

sentences.en: JANE: Well, they aren't decorative, are they, like other objects.
sentences.zh: JANE: 嗯，它们也不像其他物品那样具有装饰性，对吧？

sentences.en: Plus, nowadays, people don't keep them out on shelves as much as they used to.
sentences.zh: 而且如今，人们也不像过去那样把书摆在书架上展示了。

sentences.en: KIERAN: That's such a pity.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 这真是太可惜了。

sentences.en: When I visit someone - if they have, say, a colourful book on a table, it's the first thing I'm drawn to.
sentences.zh: 当我拜访别人时——如果他们在桌上摆着一本色彩鲜艳的书，那往往是我第一眼就会被吸引的东西。

sentences.en: JANE: I agree - and book covers can be a work of art in themselves.
sentences.zh: JANE: 我同意——书的封面本身就可以是一件艺术品。

sentences.en: Some are really eye-catching.
sentences.zh: 有些封面真的非常引人注目。

sentences.en: KIERAN: I've always been taught to handle books carefully.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 我一直被教导要小心地拿放书籍。

sentences.en: If you watch someone take a book a off a shelf, well, they usually do it wrong.
sentences.zh: 如果你观察别人从书架上取书，他们通常做法都是错的。

sentences.en: JANE: Ah, my grandfather says, you should put your hand right over the top of the book . . .
sentences.zh: JANE: 啊，我祖父说，你应该把手完全盖在书的顶部……

sentences.en: or if you can't do that, pull the other books on the shelf aside so that you can hold the whole cover.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你做不到这点，就先把书架上相邻的书挪开，以便能握住整本书的封面。

sentences.en: KIERAN: When did you learn all this?
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 你什么时候学到这些的？

sentences.en: JANE: He watched me pull a heavy book off the shelf when I was small, and it fell on the floor and broke apart.
sentences.zh: JANE: 小时候有一次，他看见我从书架上抽出一本很重的书，结果书掉到地上散开了。

sentences.en: KIERAN: Oh dear!
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 哎呀！

sentences.en: JANE: I can still remember it!
sentences.zh: JANE: 我至今还记得那一幕！

sentences.en: KIERAN: You know what I really like?
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 你知道我真正喜欢什么吗？

sentences.en: JANE: What?
sentences.zh: JANE: 什么？

sentences.en: KIERAN: The smell of new books.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 新书的味道。

sentences.en: JANE: Me too.
sentences.zh: JANE: 我也是。

sentences.en: KIERAN: My parents used to laugh at me when I was a kid because I loved putting books up to my nose.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 我小时候，父母总笑话我，因为我特别爱把书凑到鼻子跟前闻。

sentences.en: Almost as much as reading them!
sentences.zh: 几乎和读书一样喜欢！

sentences.en: JANE: New books aren't cheap, though, are they?
sentences.zh: JANE: 不过新书可不便宜，对吧？

sentences.en: KIERAN: I guess we're lucky we can buy them.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 我想我们能买得起新书，已经很幸运了。

sentences.en: JANE: My grandfather stocks second-hand books as well as new ones and they don't smell quite as good.
sentences.zh: JANE: 我祖父既经营二手书，也卖新书，但二手书的味道可没那么好。

sentences.en: KIERAN: I'd love to have a bookshop like your grandfather.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 我真希望能开一家像你祖父那样的书店。

sentences.en: What's it like?
sentences.zh: 它是什么样子的？

sentences.en: JANE: Well, it's quite big - it's got two floors and an attic, and he stocks all kinds of books really.
sentences.zh: JANE: 嗯，店挺大的——有两层楼，还有一个阁楼，他卖各种各样的书。

sentences.en: KIERAN: guess he treasures things like first ditions and other rare books.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 我猜他一定很珍视初版书和其他稀有书籍。

sentences.en: JANE: Yeah you might think he'd keep those in the attic or somewhere.
sentences.zh: JANE: 是啊，你可能会以为他会把这些书存放在阁楼之类的地方。

sentences.en: KIERAN: so they'd be hidden?
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 这样它们就藏起来了？

sentences.en: Audioscripts
sentences.zh: Audioscripts

sentences.en: JANE: Yeah.
sentences.zh: JANE: 是的。

sentences.en: But he likes people to know that he has them.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 但他希望顾客知道他有这些书。

sentences.en: So, he puts them out in the shop but makes sure you need a ladder to get them.
sentences.zh: 所以，他把它们摆在店里，但确保你得用梯子才能拿到。

sentences.en: KIERAN: Right.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 明白了。

sentences.en: That would prevent any thefts!
sentences.zh: 那样就能防止偷窃了！

sentences.en: JANE: Uhuh.
sentences.zh: JANE: 嗯。

sentences.en: KIERAN: Does he stock books for children?
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 他卖儿童读物吗？

sentences.en: JANE: He does.
sentences.zh: JANE: 卖的。

sentences.en: He particularly likes to encourage kids to read; he always says that he used to sit under the stairs as a child with a pile of books and read them all.
sentences.zh: 他尤其喜欢鼓励孩子阅读；他总说，自己小时候常坐在楼梯底下，抱着一堆书，把它们全读完。

sentences.en: KIERAN: s that where he keeps them, then?
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 那么，他就是把儿童书放在那儿喽？

sentences.en: JANE: Not exactly - he's got a dedicated area on the ground floor with cushions so that parents can enter with their toddlers, go there and spend some time reading to them.
sentences.zh: JANE: 并不完全是——他在一楼专门辟出一个区域，铺着坐垫，方便家长带着幼儿进去，陪他们一起阅读。

sentences.en: KIERAN: Oh cool.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 哦，真棒。

sentences.en: JANE: And then there's a place for pushchairs by the front door.
sentences.zh: JANE: 另外，正门口还设有婴儿车停放处。

sentences.en: And a café if anyone a if needs refreshments.
sentences.zh: 如果有人需要补充点饮料或食物，店里还有家咖啡馆。

sentences.en: KIERAN: That's good to know.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 这倒是个好消息。

sentences.en: JANE: As I said, it's a big shop and there's a storage area out the back as well.
sentences.zh: JANE: 正如我所说，这是一家很大的书店，后面还有一个储藏区。

sentences.en: KIERAN: Oh, what does he keep there?
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 哦，他在那儿都存放些什么？

sentences.en: Books he wants to throw away?
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 是打算扔掉的书吗？

sentences.en: JANE: He hardly ever throws anything away - he just leaves unwanted books by the front door for customers to take.
sentences.zh: JANE: 他几乎从不扔任何东西——只是把顾客不要的书放在正门口，供其他顾客免费取走。

sentences.en: KIERAN: Well, that's very nice.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 哇，这真是太好了。

sentences.en: JANE: Yeah - and books people or institutions have requested, they all go at the far end.
sentences.zh: JANE: 是啊——而顾客或机构订购的书籍，则全部放在最里面。

sentences.en: KIERAN: Oh.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 哦。

sentences.en: JANE: He thinks it's best to keep these out of the main shopping area as they're boxed and new.
sentences.zh: JANE: 他认为最好把这些书放在主购物区之外，因为它们是装箱的新书。

sentences.en: KIERAN: Did you get your coursebooks from him?
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 你从他那儿拿到你的课程教材了吗？

sentences.en: JANE: Naturally.
sentences.zh: JANE: 当然啦。

sentences.en: He stocks books for a lot of the colleges.
sentences.zh: 他为很多学院供应教材。

sentences.en: He used to keep these books on the first floor, but now there's a new university in my hometown, he's moved them downstairs to attract the students.
sentences.zh: 他以前把这些书放在一楼，但现在我家乡新成立了一所大学，他就把书挪到楼下，以吸引学生。

sentences.en: They're actually part of the coffee shop, on low shelves all around it.
sentences.zh: 这些书实际上属于咖啡馆的一部分，全都摆放在咖啡馆四周的矮架子上。

sentences.en: KIERAN: Pretty central then.
sentences.zh: KIERAN: 那位置相当中心啊。

sentences.en: You'll have to take me there some time!
sentences.zh: 你得找个时间带我去那儿看看！
